requirements: Customers can browse restaurant menus categorized by cuisine type, dietary restrictions, and average delivery time, with real-time updates on dish availability.

Customers can place orders by selecting items, customizing toppings, and specifying delivery instructions, with an estimated delivery time calculated based on restaurant capacity and current order queue.

Customers can track their order in real-time via a live map showing the delivery agent's location, estimated arrival time, and a step-by-step status timeline (e.g., 'Order confirmed', 'Preparing', 'Out for delivery').

Delivery agents can accept or reject incoming delivery requests based on their current location, vehicle type, and proximity to the restaurant, with the system prioritizing nearby agents for faster pickup.
Delivery agents can scan a QR code at the restaurant to confirm order pickup, triggering an automatic update to the customer's order status and updating the live map with the agent's location.
Restaurants can set dynamic menu prices based on peak hours, ingredient availability, and demand, with the system automatically adjusting prices and notifying customers of changes before checkout.
Restaurants can receive instant notifications when an order is placed, including customer details, special requests, and a countdown timer for order preparation to ensure timely delivery.

Customers can rate and tip delivery agents after order completion, with the system storing historical performance metrics (e.g., on-time delivery rate, customer ratings) for agents to build their reputation profile.
The system must process and display live order status updates within 3 seconds to ensure customers and delivery agents have real-time visibility during peak hours.
The live map tracking delivery agents must update their location every 10 seconds to maintain accuracy within 50 meters, accounting for urban GPS signal fluctuations.
The system must handle a minimum of 10,000 concurrent order placements during peak dinner hours (6 PM - 9 PM) without latency exceeding 2 seconds for order confirmation.
The restaurant menu must load within 1.5 seconds on mobile devices with a 3G connection, ensuring quick browsing even in low-bandwidth areas.
The system must store and retrieve customer order history for at least 1 year with 99.9% uptime, allowing customers to reorder past meals with one tap.
